transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because my family is really worried about how much weight I've been losing lately. To be honest, I've barely been eating anything, sometimes just one or two bites of food a day.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, and then try to get rid of it by vomiting, laxatives, or other means?
No, I don't do that at all. I never binge eat or try to throw up, and I don't use laxatives. I just focus on eating very little and keeping my food intake as restricted as possible.
Have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or a lack of interest in activities you normally enjoy?
I haven't really noticed feeling persistently sad or hopeless. I'm not really sure about that, as I've mostly just been focused on my eating and my weight.
How much importance do you place on your weight and body shape in terms of how you feel about yourself, and do you think you are currently at a healthy weight?

My weight and shape completely dictate how I feel about myself, and I am absolutely terrified of gaining even a little bit of weight. I definitely don't think I'm at a healthy weight yet, because I still feel like I need to lose more weight.
Can you tell me your current weight and height, so I can calculate your body mass index?
I don't really know my exact height, and I'd really prefer not to say my weight. Focusing on the numbers like that makes me feel extremely anxious.
Is your reluctance to share your weight and height due to fear of what the numbers might be, or is it something else that's making you anxious about discussing them?

Yes, I am absolutely terrified of the numbers. Discussing my weight makes me incredibly uncomfortable because I have an intense fear of gaining weight and feel constant, overwhelming anxiety about the scale.
I'm sorry, I think I missed what you just said. Could you please repeat your question?
Do you think you might have a problem with your eating habits or weight, or do you believe your family is overreacting to your weight loss?

I really don't think I have a problem, and I feel like my family is completely overreacting. I'm just terrified of gaining weight or getting fat, so I feel like I absolutely have to keep my weight low and control what I eat.
Do you think your body image is distorted or unrealistic in any way, or do you believe your perception of your weight and shape is accurate?

I believe my perception is completely accurate and my body image isn't distorted at all. When I look in the mirror, I still see areas where I need to lose weight, and the thought of gaining any weight is absolutely terrifying to me.

It seems like you're experiencing a strong desire to be thin, a distorted body image, and an intense fear of gaining weight. Can you tell me more about how these feelings affect your daily life and behavior?

My intense fear of gaining weight completely dominates my daily life, forcing me to constantly check the scale. To prevent any weight gain, I intentionally skip meals, strictly avoid all carbs and fats, and limit myself to tiny portions. I am just terrified that eating even a little bit of those foods will make me gain weight immediately.

There is no indication of binge eating or purging behaviors, which are characteristic of other eating disorders like Bulimia Nervosa. The patient's focus on weight and shape, and their restrictive eating patterns, further support Anorexia Nervosa as the primary diagnosis.
